notes:
Lead origin: inbound signup (free credits) — onboarding flow converted, small POC started.

Recent timeline:
- 2026-03-09: Signup + onboarding emails auto-sent (trial). curious about streaming for low-latency support replies.
- 2026-03-10: AE intro call (Priya) — high-level goals: reduce first-response time in chat, enable tool-calls for ticket lookups. Agreed to small POC (week-long).

- 2026-03-11: Follow-up notes from engineer (attached in drive). They pasted raw event stream showing partial JSON objects split across chunks.

Customer problem summary (developer notes):
- Using Hosted API streaming (server-sent events) + function-calling style. They configured function schema (name + params schema) but receive events that, when concatenated, sometimes produce trailing commas / duplicated keys. Intermittent: 1 in ~50 responses.
- Observed patterns: JSON object starts in one SSE chunk and the closing brace arrives in later chunk; their concat logic fails when chunks contain extraneous control characters (\u0000 or extra newlines).
- Sometimes streaming sends a final ephemeral "\u0007" control char before EOF which their strict JSON parser rejects.
- When not using streaming, function call payloads are valid. So likely streaming chunk boundary handling or a framing/escape bug in client SDK or their parser.

What they've tried: 
- Adjusted client concat logic to trim whitespace/newlines between chunks.
- Forced model to non-streaming mode — works but breaks latency SLA (target < 200ms median).
- Lowered temperature / deterministic sampling — no change.
- Updated to latest JS SDK — still intermittent.

Customer constraints & priorities:
- Priority: low-latency streaming for chat (median <200ms; p95 <500ms).
- Cost sensitivity: medium (SMB) — wants to stay on hosted usage pricing.
- Security: require SSO later; currently ok on default retention.

Engineering notes / recommended debugging path (from SE call):
- Reproduce with minimal repro: a tiny node script using raw fetch() to /v1/streams endpoint capturing exact bytes. Ask customer to run and paste output (not sanitized) to drive.
- Check whether client-side SSE parser is splitting on CRLF vs LF only; some SDKs buffer incorrectly and include the 'data: ' prefix in the payload passed to JSON.parse.
- Sanitize: trim leading/trailing control chars, strip BOM, remove ascii control characters prior to parse. But root cause likely generator sending an extra separator or the SDK emitting 'data:' lines without proper join.
- Compare raw bytes between streaming and non-streaming to ensure server isn't injecting control characters for heartbeat. If heartbeats are present, ensure they are emitted as separate SSE events and ignored by parser.
- If function-calling schema enforcement needed: propose using Redwood's 'strict_function_schema' toggle in POC config (SE note: feature can enforce server-side validation and emit non-streaming function call metadata as a single 'function_call' event at the end of stream).

Sales / commercial notes:
- SMB lead; likely $5k–$25k ARR if they scale from trial to 3 production teams.
- Main ask: get streaming stability so they can keep latency advantages.
- Upsell path: Dedicated pools only if they hit predictable throughput; for now hosted API OK.

Direct quotes from customer:
- "We love the latency when streaming works — but this parsing issue will block GA. We can't ship a flaky assistant."
- "If you can give us a reproducible fix in the next two weeks we'll be ready to convert."
